title: Slayyyter Slaughters Final North American Show of Scintillating Wor$t Girl in the World Tour in NYC: 5 Best Moments
summary: The fast-rising dance-pop phenom also debuted a brand new song.
contentText:
Slayyyter is on top of the world right now, and her two-night stint in NYC this weekend showed why.

On Saturday (Oct. 3) and Sunday (Oct. 4), the Missouri-born pop star mounted the final North American shows of her ongoing Wor$t Girl in the World tour at Terminal 5 and Brooklyn Paramount, respectively. Backed by an impressively tight band and a set that brought to life key music video motifs and imagery from her Wor$t Girl in America era, Slayyyter slayed her Brooklyn show, delivering roof-raising vocals, crisp hairography (another star student of Sasha Fierce has emerged), snazzy costume changes and rollicking arrangements that amped up the electro-punk -meets-nu-metal backbone of her breakthrough LP.

Standing at a healthy 21 tracks, Slayyyter’s tour setlist features all 14 songs from Wor$t Girl in America , with the only additional tracks (“Nekromantic,” “Hymn” and “I Think He’s Got a Girl”) being peeks at that record’s forthcoming “brother album,” Wor$t Man in America . Of course, she also performs her remix of Turnstile’s “Birds” and “Broke B—h Freestyle,” an unreleased track she’s played live for years and finally dropped as a surprise standalone single shortly after the release of Wor$t Girl .

If the setlist didn’t make it clear, then Slayyyter’s art direction and costume design certainly underscored that she’s truly all-in on this Wor$t Girl/Man in America era. She didn’t play any full songs from earlier in her catalog — that’s two albums, one mixtape and one EP’s worth of material! — and barely bantered with the crowd, opting instead to tear through her setlist with raging, sexy rockstar energy. From the general Midwest gothic feel of her immersive set to the trailer park Playbunny costumes, Slayyyter has fine-tuned one of the most visually alluring and intellectually interesting aesthetics in contemporary pop music — and she’s only interested in exploring that realm at the moment. That level of commitment — let alone the intense physicality of her stage show — is what makes Slayyyter such a compelling pop performer and such a fresh presence in the space.

And, of course, Wor$t Girl in America still sounds as rich and explosive in October as it did upon its release this spring. The album arrived on March 27 via Columbia Records, debuting atop Dance Albums and reaching No. 22 on the Billboard 200 . Two of the album’s singles reached the Dance/Pop Songs chart: “Dance…” (No. 7) and “Crank” (No. 12), the latter of which earned a sequel titled “Crank 2” last month. Both “Crank 2” and “Brand New Chanel$” — which marked her first appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 (No. 98) — will appear on Wor$t Man in America , a project Slayyyter describes as a “ deeper, more emotional,” eight-track “inverse album ,” though not all the songs are direct flips of Wor$t Girl tracks.

The Wor$t Girl in the World Tour resumes on Oct. 18 at Paris’ Le Trianon. The trek’s European leg will take Slayyyter to major cities such as Prague, Berlin and Manchester before concluding on Nov. 5 at London’s Roundhouse.

From Finnish electronic duo Pearly Drops kicking off the night with its cinematic opening set to the rousing finale of “Beat Up Chanel$,” the Wor$t Girl in the World Tour North American finale was one of the year’s most thrilling pop shows.

Here are the five best moments of Slayyyter’s Wor$t Girl in the World Tour stop in Brooklyn, New York.
